title: Famous Door sextet with Jimmy Hamilton and Dizzy Gillespie
summary: At the Famous Door he led a sextet with Hamilton and Gillespie, who he hired after hearing him with Calloway.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with and understanding Thelonious Monk

blocks.x: And then of course, that was where you played with Jimmy Hamilton on the clarinet?
Yes, Jimmy Hamilton. On clarinet.
And that was at Kelly Stables.
That's right.
And did he go with you to the Famous Door, too?
Actually, I think Jimmy Hamilton played with me at the Famous Door rather than Kelly Stables. Yes.
Right. And then, of course, we remember that Dizzie Gillespie joined you at the famous Door, right?
That's right ... in a sextet I had.
Right. Do you remember any of the others who played in that group?
Did Teddy Wilson play in that group?
I don't think so. I don't have ...
You know, I can't remember. I can't remember. I think there was Charlie Drayton on bass.
Uh huh. Was Jonah Jones in with you at any point in there?
Yes, but Jonah played with the Big Band.
Uh huh.
Jonah played with me in the Big Band.
I think that may have been the band where you toured, right? And you played this date in
Syracuse where Billy Holiday was on. I think you played in that group, didn't you?
I think so. Was that 1942?
Yes. Well, then that was after the Famous Door, yes.
After the Famous Door. At the Famous Door, how was it -- how was it with Dizzie? How did Dizzie come to join you? Do you recall that? Of course, you knew him very well over the years.
Yes. He'd been with Cab Calloway, and I liked what he was doing, and I asked him if he would join me ...
And he did.
He did.
Simple as that?
Simple as that!
How did -- now, was he playing what has become known, at least not among musicians, let's say -- but among fans -- as the new style? Bop was well under way by 1942, of course.
Yes.
Now you had come up and had been accustomed to playing in a certain way. But do you remember at the time any question of adjustment or Dizzie adjusting?
Well, the only thing that I recall was that Dizzie did his thing and I did my thing, and you know?
So far as you knew, youwere both concerned, you went very well together?
Yeah, that's all, sure. It was all music, you know.
